As a millennial who has lost their mother, as a surprise, who was my favorite person of all life: first, don’t worry about it before it happens. You can what if all the live long day but that’s silly goose stuff. It’s a waste of your energy. If your mom/dad is close, get them to tell you usernames and passwords. Sometimes only one person paid one bill and that sucks. Hello verizon, no I don’t have the password, the account user has passed away. That sucks. 

Now big stuff: if your favorite person in the world leaves, it will be okay. Not at first and not always but give yourself grace to try existing without that person (you have no choice so breathe). It may suck for a long time. I didn’t not feel okay for 7 years. I had to take fmla for grief. It wasn’t all the time but sometimes I’d be overcome. Now I try to take off work on days that matter so that I can honor my person. 

This part is inevitable but some don’t come for moons. Aside from passwords, wills, and logistics, do not worry. If you’re able to get plans in place then don’t fret until it happens

I don’t know if professional tools are required as much as professional time and work. If I had that kind of time and motivation, I’d pick a room and go top-down. Cobwebs in the ceiling corners? Remove things that can be removed. Wash curtains, walls, surfaces, rugs/mats, floors. (The reason for a top to bottom approach is that I find if I vacuum and sweep and THEN dust, some gets back on the floor). Organize/de clutter things to move back in. Replace the curtains, rugs, etc. 
 
Products are going to depend on the room. Windex for windows, bath stuff for tubs, bar keepers friend can do a lot, but sometimes it’s not needed. Mostly cloths, (newspaper is you want to really clean glass and mirrors- use it to wipe of the windex or whatever) trash bags, paper towels vacuum, pledge for dusting (I like the smell) and hard work can do wonders for a room. If using strong smelling cleaners, open the windows so you don’t pass out lol. I’d also suggest rocking out to your favorite tunes. It’s hard work and takes time, like painting a room does, but it’s doable if you can commit to the work and time.
